text:
maya: heads up — sampleapp batcher started returning mixed-dim vectors in rerank flow after a retry loop triggered yesterday
kevin: ugh. mixed how? 1536 vs 1024?
maya: yep. most requests are 1024 per model config but when the client retry path replays an in-flight batch we sometimes get a response shape that looks like 1536 for some items
sam: any traceback? logs?
maya: pasted minimal trace from local repro:
```
2026-03-22T15:12:03Z batch_id=bb-42 attempt=1 POST /v1/embeddings -> 200 ids=10 dims=1024
2026-03-22T15:12:03Z batch_id=bb-42 attempt=2 POST /v1/embeddings -> 200 ids=10 dims=1536
```
alex: that implies two different model variants being routed. Are retries hitting a fallback model?
kevin: also could be a different response key mapping. sampleapp expects `embedding` but node SDK returns `embeddings` array; any mapping code that reshuffles arrays on retry?
maya: this is the weird bit — we see identical request bodies (same input order & ids), but the retry code in the sampleapp's batching helper does a naive concat when merging partial responses if shapes differ, which ends up producing 1536-length vectors (1024 + 512) in some items :face_with_rolling_eyes:
sam: ahhh. concat bug in client-side merge. So it's not model drift, it's merge logic creating longer vectors by appending a second partial embedding.
kevin: do we have the helper code snippet?
maya: here's the helper snippet that was causing it:
```
// pseudo
function mergeResponses(base, partial) {
  return base.map((b, i) => {
    if (!partial[i]) return b;
    return b.concat(partial[i]); // <- bad: assumes these are different segments
  });
}
```
alex: yeah that's the culprit. Retry should replace or pick the latest, not concat. Also need to validate dims before merging.
kevin: quick fix: if dims differ, throw and trigger a safe fallback to re-request whole batch, or enforce `idempotency-key` so the server dedupes and returns consistent shard responses
maya: i pushed a hotfix to sampleapp to detect dim mismatch and bail instead of concatenating. PR: https://git.internal/redwood/sampleapp/pull/789
sam: for SDK parity: python helper had a stricter merge that raised on mismatch; node helper inherited older behavior. Let's add a parity test in devex harness.
kevin: also saw auth/retry interplay — our retry wrapper was reusing the same `batch_id` header but not the same `request_id`, causing some routing heuristics to select different model variants in SmartRouting (cost tier fallback). We should consistently set `x-request-group` and `x-batch-id` across retries
alex: can we add a lightweight CI test that simulates a partial response then a retry that returns different shape, assert client throws and doesn't produce corrupted vector?
sam: yes. I'll add an e2e that injects a fake partial response from the test server and asserts the merge step rejects it.
ci-bot: pipeline triggered: devex/embedding-batcher-parity-check -> started
maya: follow-up items:
- add dim validation in batching helper (throw on mismatch)
- add parity test across node/python helpers
- document expected response keys (`embedding` vs `embeddings`) in sampleapp onboarding note
- ensure idempotency headers are consistent across retries (x-batch-id + x-request-group)
kevin: note for docs: example fix snippet for users failing into this:
```
// validate dims
if (embedding.length !== expectedDim) {
  throw new Error(`Embedding dimension mismatch: got ${embedding.length} expected ${expectedDim}`)
}
```
maya: also adding a debug flag to the helper to log original batch order + ids before merge so ops can triage quickly
alex: thanks — super useful. Can we also update the SDK changelog so customers who vendored the helper know about the change (it's breaking if they relied on concat)
maya: good call. I'll add an entry under "embedding-batcher: stricter merge semantics"
sam: once tests pass we should roll to staging and run sampleapp smoke for rerank pages
kevin: assigned: sam for tests, maya for hotfix + docs, alex for changelog. ETA EOD tomorrow?
maya: EOD works for me
kevin: thx. :thumbsup:
